title: New England Conservatory and liking all kinds of music
summary: In Boston he studied at the New England Conservatory for three and a half years. He says all music is good when played well.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I played the mix of land, I played swing, and here's this modern jazz coming, says everybody's going to study. I says, well, I'm going to join the rest of them. He says, nothing to do. I didn't do anything in the daytime, so I went on studying. I wound up three and a half years in New England Conservatory, see? And that's why I had very good training. So then we played, I played, it was progressive music. As a matter of fact, I like all music, all types of music. It's all good when it's played good. That's right. Most people will ask you, what do you like? You like this jazz better? They're like, it's all good when it's played good. That's right. Because Dixieland, they have good Dixieland, they have bad Dixieland. I've heard some Dixieland bands, it's terrible. I know some guy probably will eat my head off, but it's true. Never overestimate. No, no, it's true. I've heard some bad swing. I've heard some bad progressive jazz. And it's rock and roll, everything. I like it all, as long as it's good. Because that soul of music, regardless what type of music there is, I played lots of semi-classics in the school symphonies, you know. See what's going. And it's just good music. Once you're a musician, you get that in your soul, and your love, love of music. You've got to learn to love any type, and know it.
